points.description: States that an SVM is a (in the simplest case linear) classifier that separates the classes using a decision boundary (hyperplane) chosen to have the maximum margin. Equivalent wording accepted, e.g. 'widest-street separating hyperplane'.
Identifies support vectors as the data points closest to (on or near) the decision boundary, and says they determine the margin/boundary.
States that kernels (the kernel trick) are used so that an SVM can separate data that are not linearly separable.
States that training an SVM (finding the maximum-margin boundary) is solved as a quadratic programming (QP) optimisation problem.
